**66,37,7d** What sort of food, then, are we going to eat after the resurrection of the dead?

**66,37,7e** For if after the resurrection Jesus ate a second time, both a part of a broiled fish and some honeycomb, and lodged with the disciples over forty days, will there not then be eating?

**66,37,7f** And concerning eating it is clear: “Blessed is the one who will eat bread in the kingdom of the heavens”.

**66,37,7g** And there is the promise of the Lord himself, that “you shall be sitting at the table of my Father, eating and drinking”.

**66,37,7h** And the eating and drinking is known to him alone, since “what eye has not seen and ear has not heard, nor has it gone up into the heart of man, all that God has prepared for those who love him”.

**66,37,7i** But since we have reached this passage, setting out the differences of souls, and the things that come from the truth itself, and the example being complete — that the soul of a man is one thing and that of a beast another, and that he came to save not the soul of the beast but that of the man, because beasts are not judged.

**66,37,7j** For men inherit the kingdom of heaven, and men are judged.

**66,37,7k** For “the ones will depart into eternal judgment, and the others into eternal life,” says the Only-begotten.

**66,40,1a** And what of those who pry into questions?

**66,40,1b** When they come upon a text and do not grasp its plain sense, they are vexed, devising contradictions for themselves rather than hunting out what is useful for themselves, since Matthew says “two demoniacs”, while Luke tells of one.

**66,40,2** For indeed one of the evangelists says that the robbers who were crucified with him reviled him, while the other not only indicates that the two did not both revile him, but also tells of the defence made by the one.

**66,40,3a** For he rebuked the other, and said, “You do not fear God, though we are under the same sentence; but this holy one has done nothing.”

**66,40,3b** And besides this he called out, saying, “Remember me, Jesus, when you come in your kingdom.”

**66,40,3c** And the Saviour said to him, “Amen, I say to you, today you shall be with me in paradise.”

**66,40,4a** Now these things seem to involve a disagreement in Scripture.

**66,40,4b** But all things are smooth.

**66,40,5a** For even if in Matthew there are two demoniacs, in Luke they are the same.

**66,40,5b** But since Scripture is accustomed to give the reasons for what was done, for this reason Luke makes mention not of the two, but of the one.

**66,40,6a** For there were two who were healed of the demons, but one remained in the faith, while the other ran aground.

**66,40,6b** Because of his remaining in the faith, then, he followed Jesus, as the gospel has it, to whatever place he went.

**66,40,6c** For this reason he passed over the one, and made mention of the one who belongs to the kingdom of the heavens.

**66,40,6d** And nothing stands in contradiction to the finding of the truth.

**66,41,1a** And indeed the gospel relates another occasion similar to this matter, as though concerning one.

**66,41,1b** The Lord cleansed ten lepers, and the nine went away and did not give glory to God, but the one returned and remained, he who was also praised by the Lord, according as he said, “Ten lepers were cleansed.

**66,41,1c** Why did not one of them return to give glory to God, but only this foreigner?”

**66,41,2a** And you see that because of the one man’s quickness of feeling and his deed of gratitude he makes mention of him instead of the ten.

**66,41,2b** So likewise, since the one evangelist made mention of robbers.

**66,41,3a** For we are accustomed to speak of singular things in the plural and of plural things in the singular.

**66,41,3b** For we say, “We have related to you,” and “we have beheld you,” and “we are here among you,” whereas those speaking are not two, but one is present, and that one, by the custom of usage, speaks plurally, in the person of many.

**66,41,4** So the account in the gospel has included it in the plural, while the other relates that one was the blasphemer, and the other confessed and obtained salvation.

**66,41,5** And you see how all the things of the truth are clear, and there is nothing contradictory in Scripture.

**66,41,6a** But in going through all these things in Scripture we have drawn out the narrative of our discourse to some breadth, I think.

**66,41,6b** And may it be that we toil at the breadth of our discourse, but refute those who are against the truth, and gladden her sons through the healing remedies of the truth.

**66,42,1a** Then again, let us look at the charlatan’s other notions; for he says that the two covenants are contrary to one another, and that the God who gave utterance in the Law is other than the God of the gospel.

**66,42,1b** And to the former he gives the name of archon, while the Son, and the Father, he calls his own good God.

**66,42,1c** And would that he spoke the truth, and did not, in his error, blaspheme against himself.

**66,42,2a** With this same statement we ourselves also agree: that the good Father’s good offspring, light from light, God from God, true God from true God, came to us to save us.

**66,42,2b** “He came to his own, and not to what was another’s.

**66,42,2c** His own did not receive him.

**66,42,3** But to all who received him he gave authority to become God’s children, who were begotten not from blood nor from flesh, but from God.”

**66,42,4a** And yet no one in the world was born without flesh and blood, but all have become partakers of flesh and blood.

**66,42,4b** For what were they before their birth in the flesh, or what are we able to be without flesh?

**66,42,5a** But since the world came into being from God, and we, being created, have been born of the flesh of our fathers and mothers, the Lord came to give us birth from Spirit and fire.

**66,42,5b** For we were born, and no one can deny the first birth, nor that we are of flesh.

**66,42,6** But in the second birth we have been born not of flesh, nor of blood — that is, not as making use of the misuse of the flesh and of the blood — but as having been born in spirit, flesh and soul, no longer being fleshly, but blood and flesh and soul spiritually united;

**66,42,7** that is, “he gave them power to become children of God,” to those who change their mind and have pleased God through flesh and blood and soul.

**66,42,8a** He, then, who came to his own is not a stranger, but the Master of all.

**66,42,8b** And for this reason he says, “He who speaks in the prophets: behold, I am here”.

**66,42,8c** And to the Jews he said, “If you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote of me”.

**66,42,8d** And, “Abraham your father exulted to see my day; and he saw, and rejoiced.”

**66,42,9a** And, “So your fathers did to the prophets,” and, “Blessed are you when they revile you and speak every evil against you falsely.

**66,42,9b** Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven.

**66,42,9c** For so they persecuted the prophets who were before you”.

**66,42,9d** And at another time, “Jerusalem, that kills the prophets and stones the ones who have been sent, how many times have I wished to gather your children?”

**66,42,10a** And the “how often” shows that he took care to gather her through prophets.

**66,42,10b** For if he says reprovingly, “who kills the prophets”, then he takes care for the prophets.

**66,42,10c** And he who cares for the prophets was not caring for strangers, but for his own.

**66,42,11** “And there shall be required,” he says, “the blood that is shed, from the blood of Abel to Zacharias the righteous, who was poured out between the temple and the altar.

**66,42,12a** And taking up everything, he upset the money-changers’ tables too, and said, ‘Do not make my Father’s house a house of trade.’”

**66,42,12b** And he said to Mary and Joseph, “How is it that you were looking for me?

**66,42,12c** Did you not know that I must be in what is my Father’s?”

**66,42,12d** And at once the gospel adds, saying that he said, “Do not make my Father’s house a house of trade,” as it says, “And the disciples called to mind that it had been written, ‘Zeal for your house has devoured me’”.

**66,43,1a** And how much there is to say, through such passages of the gospels and of the apostles, for the refutation of Mani’s mania?

**66,43,1b** And how he wishes to divide and estrange the Old Testament from the New, though the Old bears witness concerning the Saviour and the Saviour acknowledges the Old Testament — and not only he, but the apostles themselves too —

**66,43,2a** as David says, “The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right hand.’

**66,43,2b** If then he calls him Lord, how is he his son?”

**66,43,3a** And again in another place it says, “When the children cried ‘Hosanna to the Son of David’,” and he did not rebuke them, the Pharisees say, “Do you not hear what these are saying?

**66,43,3b** Stop them”.

**66,43,3c** And he said to them, “If these are silent, the stones will cry out”.

**66,43,4a** For he is the son of David according to the flesh, but the Lord of David according to the Spirit, both expressions being valid and true.

**66,43,4b** For nothing is counterfeit in the truth.

**66,43,5a** But so as not to lengthen this subject, I shall be content with these testimonies, and shall go on to the other matters, refuting the charlatan.

**66,43,5b** If the body is of one god, you there, and the soul of another god, what fellowship do the two have?

**66,43,6a** And I am afraid, seeing into how great a mass of the depth of thoughts the small mind of our littleness is trying to stoop and peer.

**66,43,6b** So I shall rein myself in, so as not to cause much labour of reading to those who are able to refute the sorcerer even from a single testimony.

**66,43,7a** For sharing together in the same thing does not belong to those who are at variance with one another, but it is the work of one, or the labour of two friends.

**66,43,7b** Since the body and the soul, then, are together in the same thing, it is the work of one God.

**66,43,7c** For there is no division, since both work together fittingly and give glory together.

**66,43,8a** But if, according to his account, the archons devoured the soul and made this body a bond for it, how do they afterwards shut up in a body the soul that has been eaten?

**66,43,8b** For everything that is eaten is consumed, and what is consumed passes into non-existence.

**66,43,8c** And what passes into non-existence and no longer is, is neither enclosed in any place, nor is there, nor will there be, a place of imprisonment for that which does not exist.

**66,44,1a** And often, forgetting his own mind, he forgets what he may have said, and the very things he once constructs he unwittingly demolishes again.

**66,44,1b** For at one time he speaks of the soul that was eaten, laying it down that it is shut up in existing bodies, and at another he lays it down that the same soul was snatched away by the archons from above, out of the panoply of the good God, so that it was no longer eaten but taken captive.

**66,44,2** And at another time he no longer speaks consistently of this same soul that was taken captive, but relates the account of it in another way,

**66,44,3** saying that it was deliberately cast out as bait by the power above, in the manner of a young goat cast into a pit for trapping the wild beast, so that the beast, excited, comes down to take the kid, and is itself caught.

**66,44,4** And if the power above — this being the good God, or else the light, as he himself names it — sent the kid from its own power, then even if it catches the beast, the kid will first be devoured meanwhile, and the power above will rather harm itself, throwing down a portion of itself to be the beast’s food, so that it may seem to catch the beast by means of a part through which it itself suffers loss;

**66,44,5** and it no longer overpowers the beast by word or will as one strong and supreme and mighty, but contrives in many ways and plays the knave, so as to be able to get the better of the beast.

**66,44,6** And if the beast should be caught at all, it has already lost from its own portion the kid that was eaten, even if it should be able to catch it at all.

**66,44,7** For if the power above sent the soul here, so as to fetter the principalities and the authorities by hunting them through the soul, the aim did not turn out for her who so planned.

**66,44,8a** For even if it sent the soul to hunt, it has been hunted; or to snare, it has been snared, having come from a pure nature and fallen first under the bond of a body of matter, and then also under many absurdities of sins.

**66,44,8b** And on every side the deceiver’s account and the wretch’s teaching fall to pieces.

**66,45,1a** Come, then, let us look also at the Mother of Life, the power which he says was put forth.

**66,45,1b** And the Mother of Life herself, and the First Man, the five elements, which are, as he says, wind, light, water, fire and matter.

**66,45,2a** And that he, having put these on as equipment for war, went down below and made war on the darkness.

**66,45,2b** For the archons of the darkness, warring against him, ate of his panoply, which is the soul.

**66,45,3** Oh, the charlatan’s mime-talk! Oh, the incomparable mockery and the laughable system, whose outcome on every side attaches weakness to God, and on every side assigns ignorance to God who knows all things!

**66,45,4** For he who, according to his account, put forth the Mother of Life bears reproach, either because he was ignorant of what would be accomplished by the Mother of Life, or because the events, having turned out contrary to the expectation of his mind, were found to be otherwise.

**66,45,5** For he would stand convicted of ignorance who thought that one thing would come about, but found afterwards that another had happened, not according to his will.

**66,45,6a** For the Mother of Life, called by him a power, put forth from him — how shameful it is even to speak of a Mother of Life!

**66,45,6b** For it is not admitted by those who possess sound reasoning to conceive of anything female in the Godhead.

**66,45,7a** And this female, he says, put forth the First Man; and, in a word, he imagines the First Man in his nature, and the Mother of Life, from the things that happen among us.

**66,45,7b** For on earth there is one who is called man, and a mother who bore us from the earth, she who was created by God for Adam.

**66,45,8** And the brutish man imagines from his own reasonings that there are in heaven such things as there are also on earth, which it does not admit, as the divine word teaches throughout.

**66,45,9a** For it speaks of heavenly bodies and earthly bodies.

**66,45,9b** But the glory of the heavenly is one, and that of the earthly another; and it has not yet described at all the things above the heavens, but spoke of these visible things that are body — I mean the sun, or the moon, or the things on earth — and of the bodies of the saints, as at least we, being lowly, understand it.

**66,45,10a** And if the statement should also concern the things above heaven, because of the very deep capacity of knowledge in the apostle himself, we do not lay it down absolutely.

**66,45,10b** Nevertheless, they have been spoken of as far above earthly things; by how much more, then, the things beyond the heavens?

**66,45,10c** How can they be likened to earthly things, you there?

**66,46,1** And as for the First Man, who, you say again, furnished himself with the wind, the light, the fire, the water and the matter by way of a panoply —

**66,46,2** then, if the First Man is from above and came here to furnish himself with the panoply, and to put it forth for himself as his breastplate and his strengthening, the things in this world are more powerful than the one of the heavenly beings who came from above.

**66,46,3** For the water is the water that is seen, and the light the light that appears, and matter that which according to you perishes, and the wind that which sounds among us, and the fire this fire which we all use freely for our needs.

**66,46,4a** And if he wars on the archons with such things, what is the operation of the war, tell me: who might sound the trumpet for us, becoming leader of the war?

**66,46,4b** Let us divide the phalanxes, let us draw up the wings of the battle.

**66,46,5** Who might shoot the first arrow against the one so grievously maddened, against the substance of the principalities and authorities?

**66,46,6a** Does wind make war, you there?

**66,46,6b** Or matter, which according to you perishes?

**66,46,6c** Or the fire which was made by the Lord for our use?

**66,46,6d** Or the light, which gives way to the darkness in turn, the intervals of the times having been ordained by God?

**66,46,6e** Or the water?

**66,46,6f** In what way?

**66,46,7a** Relate the empty babblings you utter.

**66,46,7b** For indeed we see both good and bad things done by means of these.

**66,46,7c** For in fire sacrifices are made to idols, and the fire does not refuse, nor does it prevent the sin.

**66,46,7d** Those who worship demons pour libations with the water of the sea, and he who tries to commit an act of ignorance in water has never been prevented.

**66,46,8a** And how many pirates have committed murders on the waters of the sea?

**66,46,8b** And the water, rather, is no enemy of the archons of wickedness, as you claim, but rather works along with them — though the water is not the cause, but each man is the cause of his own sin.

**66,46,9a** And oh, your great drivel!

**66,46,9b** And what did the equipment of weapons and the breastplate of the elements profit the First Man — according to you — who came down to make war and was worn down by the darkness?

**66,46,10** For you say that the Man was afflicted down there, and that when he prayed the Father heard him, as you said, and sent another power put forth by him, called the Living Spirit.

**66,46,11a** Take off your mask, you comic poet Menander!

**66,46,11b** For you are that man, and you cover yourself up, relating the deeds of adulterers and of drunkenness; for nothing in you stands firm.

**66,46,11c** For by bringing in the poems of the Greeks in place of the truth you lead astray those who have been deceived by you.

**66,46,12a** For perhaps Hesiod showed more sense than you when he related his poetic compositions on the generation of the gods; perhaps Orpheus; perhaps Euripides.

**66,46,12b** For even if they told laughable things, it is plain that, being poets, they composed things that are not; but you relate them as things that are, so as to make the error greater.

**66,47,1** You say that this Living Spirit came down below and gave its right hand, and brought up out of the darkness the one you call the First Man, who was in peril down below in the lower regions — he who came down to save the devoured soul and was not able to save it, but was himself put in peril.

**66,47,2** For though he was sent for salvation he fell into peril, and in his turn stood in need of another envoy for his own salvation.

**66,47,3a** How much more, then, would the soul be in peril, for whose sake the First Man who was sent came and fell into peril?

**66,47,3b** But there was also a second envoy sent to save, which you yourself say is the Living Spirit.

**66,47,4a** So it was out of regret that the Father sent the one who was stronger still, that he might become the saviour of the First Man.

**66,47,4b** Or was he unaware that the first was powerless, and, supposing that he would save, when that one fell into peril did he learn afterwards by experience, and so put forth and send another?

**66,47,5** Great indeed is the absurdity, Manichaean, and incoherent is the drivel of your whole teaching.

**66,47,6a** Again he says that the Spirit came down and gave its right hand, and brought up the First Man who had been in peril.

**66,47,6b** For this reason he has handed down a mystery to his disciples: to give one another the right hand whenever they meet, as a sign, as men saved from darkness.

**66,47,7a** For he says that everything is in the darkness except himself alone.

**66,47,7b** For the blind too, by way of mockery rather, are called “keen-sighted” by those who see, who shun the ill-omened word.

**66,48,1a** Then he says again — contriving for us some further constructions and feats of architecture, as though he had been present there, and imagining things that do not exist — that at that time this Living Spirit, he says, created the world.

**66,48,1b** And it put on three other powers, came down and brought up the rulers, and fixed them in the firmament, which is their sphere.

**66,48,2** And as for its bringing them up — the brutish man does not even perceive how he fights against himself, blaming what he himself praises and turning what is blamed into praise, like a man who is drunk and reeling and babbling one thing in place of another.

**66,48,3** For he says that the rulers, being down below in the darkness, are of an evil substance, and that the region is one of corruption.

**66,48,4** And if the Spirit, using force, brought the rulers up to the regions above out of this corruption and out of the portion of the darkness, for punishment rather, and in making their removal from base places dragged them up to the regions above for punishment, then the regions above will no longer be good and of a life-giving substance, but rather of death.

**66,48,5** And the regions below will no longer be punishment, but of some good substance — the place from which the Spirit, wishing to transfer the rulers into punishment, moved them away from what was pleasant and needful to the place of punishment, so that it might punish them in this way.

**66,48,6a** And besides, if the Spirit has made the world, how can you say, on the other hand, that the world did not come into being by God?

**66,48,6b** And if the firmament is the body of the rulers, on what sort of cross, then, did it nail the rulers?

**66,48,6c** For at one time you say that they have been fixed in the firmament, and at another you define the firmament itself as their body.

**66,48,7a** Great is the incoherence of your words, which has no consistency with the truth.

**66,48,7b** How you have come against us as an enemy in everything — or rather against yourself and those who receive your opinion!

**66,49,1a** Next this same man says once more that, when it had crucified the rulers in the sphere, it created the luminaries, which are the remnant of the soul.

**66,49,1b** And he does not say the soul, but remnants of the soul.

**66,49,2a** O incoherent doctrine, O false and disjointed words!

**66,49,2b** For every remnant is a part of the whole, and the whole is greater than the remnant.

**66,49,3** If, then, the luminaries are the remnants, let him show us something greater than the luminaries, so that we may see the soul.

**66,49,4** But if the whole has been devoured and consumed and the luminaries are a remnant, then they too, being beneath the crucified rulers, will be devoured, since the rulers hold the higher place.

**66,49,5** But if, because they have been crucified, they can no longer have the soul and the luminaries in their grip, your drivelling account has collapsed, Manichaean.

**66,49,6a** Then again the same man teaches that after the rebuke given to the Omophorus, matter too, he says, created all the plants for itself; and when these were being plundered by the rulers, the great ruler called all the rulers, the foremost among them too, and took one power from each of them, and fashioned a man after the pattern of that First Man, and in him he bound the soul.

**66,49,6b** This is the basis of the commingling.

**66,49,7a** And since the Living Father, he says, saw the soul afflicted in the body, being compassionate and merciful he sent his beloved Son for the salvation of the soul.

**66,49,7b** For it was on this pretext, he says, and on that of the Omophorus, that he was sent.

**66,49,8** And the Son came and refashioned himself into the likeness of a human being, and he was seen by men as a man, and men assumed that he had been born.

**66,49,9a** So when he had come and carried out the work of fashioning, he constructed for the salvation of men a machine with twelve buckets, which, turned by the sphere, draws up the souls of the dying.

**66,49,9b** And the great luminary takes them with its rays, purifies them and hands them on to the moon; and in this way the disc of the moon, as it is called among us, is filled.

**66,50,1a** And do you see how great is the drivelling nonsense of this charlatan, and the forgetfulness of his drunkenness?

**66,50,1b** For he consigns what he says to forgetfulness, and whatever he appears to say he remodels and dismantles, overthrowing his own doctrines, telling it now one way and now another; his later statements overthrow his first, and what he overthrew at first he builds up again,

**66,50,2** as if to show that he is not in his own control but, driven by an unclean spirit, tells one thing in place of another, like those who are delirious.

**66,50,3** For if he means the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, that coming took place many years after the luminaries came into being, and after what he calls the machine of the twelve buckets.

**66,50,4a** For the stars have been in heaven continually ever since they came into being, whether they wish to call them elements or intervals and measures of the heaven.

**66,50,4b** At all events, from the fourth day of the making of the world all things have been well ordered, not to the harm of the things over which God is Lord.

**66,50,5** But the coming of Christ began its preaching in the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar, after the thirtieth year from his birth, which came to the five thousand five hundredth year from the making of the world and the thirtieth of his age, and the thirty-third up to the cross.

**66,50,6a** How, then, were these things, both luminaries and stars, in heaven from the first?

**66,50,6b** But if he says that he came before this and made these things, his nonsense does not hold together; for before there was a man on the earth there came into being what he calls the elements, and the twelve buckets so called to no purpose, and the machine with which he means to beguile, by pleasing names, those whom he has led astray.

**66,51,1** For to anyone possessed of understanding it is evident from the very wording of Scripture and its order that all the stars and the luminaries came into being on the fourth day, before Adam, the first-formed man, was fashioned.

**66,51,2** But this man says that he came, he says, to make the twelve buckets in human form, and showed himself to men as a man; and, though ignorant even of the order of things established from the beginning, he thinks he is saying something, and like a blind man guiding himself he leads those whom he has blinded along paths that run on into lies.

**66,51,3a** But when the truth is present and opens the eyes through those of understanding, it turns his drivel into laughter.

**66,51,3b** For to what men did he appear, when they did not exist?

**66,51,3c** And how did he who took no body appear in the form of a man?

**66,51,4** And if in the coming in the flesh he accomplished this by appearing without being, then the events were a semblance.

**66,51,5a** Then he has not appeared, nor did he come.

**66,51,5b** For if, when he had come, he was not, then he did not come in the first place.

**66,51,5c** And if he was taken for a man, yet a man he was not, what was it that urged the Word of God to show himself as a man though he was none?

**66,51,5d** Unless perhaps, being dragged off by creditors, he wished to disguise himself in a form, so that he might escape the notice of those who were looking for him.

**66,51,6a** And if he both appeared and was not, what sort of truth was this?

**66,51,6b** For in truth there is no falsehood, even as the Only-begotten declares concerning himself, “It is I who am the truth and the life.”

**66,51,6c** And life has no death, and truth could not undergo alteration, lest by disturbing the truth it should no longer be truth.

**66,51,7a** And his theatrical scheme has collapsed on every count.

**66,51,7b** For neither were the stars created after the coming, nor were there men before the stars came into being.

**66,51,7c** And on this side and on that the deceiver Manichaeus stands refuted, as I have already shown above.

**66,52,1a** Concerning his theory of the moon, he says that its disc is filled from the souls.

**66,52,1b** But before a man died on the earth, from where was the disc filled?

**66,52,1c** For after Adam’s life had run to its nine hundred and thirtieth year, how did the one soul, the first to die on the earth, fill the disc?

**66,52,2** Or how could the nine hundred and thirty years be named years and times at all, unless the moon was waxing and waning and completing the course appointed for it, receiving its fullness not from souls, but having from God the command of his wisdom?

**66,52,3** And all living creatures, he says, are filled with the same soul — so that he may put on a level the soul of a man and of a mouse and of a worm and of the other bodies of lowly formation.

**66,52,4** As for the rest of his nonsense — how the virgin appears to the rulers, now in the shape of a man and now in that of a woman — perhaps picturing the hermaphrodite of his own demon he is setting forth his own passions of lust.

**66,52,5** Then he says that whenever the great ruler is despoiled by the so-called virgin, he puts forth his clouds and causes pestilence, and begins to cut the roots, and in this way death comes about.

**66,52,6** And the brutish man did not see that what he calls death, and blames, he ought rather to call life, because the souls are released from bodies.

**66,52,7a** And if the rulers regard the soul’s being in a body as a prison at all, then on his own account the ruler would never do this, so as to release from prison the soul that he holds.

**66,52,7b** And how great is the absurdity in this trickster’s teaching?

**66,53,1a** The rest is full of mockery, such as their so-called elect.

**66,53,1b** And in reality they have been elected by the devil for condemnation, that the saying might be fulfilled, “And his food is elect.”

**66,53,2** For they sit like drones and do no work, but are busybodies, not even knowing that it is against them that the holy apostle makes his proclamation — speaking as one who knew, as by prophecy, that certain men would come, not from the teaching of God but thunderstruck by the devil, idle and self-willed in evil,

**66,53,3** he says, “Whoever does not work, let him not eat either,” so as to brand as counterfeit the scheme of these idlers.

**66,53,4a** So they bid their catechumens feed them lavishly.

**66,53,4b** And these bring every necessity of any kind to their elect, so that each may be seen, forsooth, to be pious in feeding the chosen souls.

**66,53,5a** And they, on receiving it — it is laughable to say — under the pretext of praying for those who brought it, rather lay something close to a curse on them, bearing witness against them to wickedness rather than goodness; for they say this: “I neither sowed you nor reaped you; I did not grind, nor did I throw into the oven.”

**66,53,5b** “Another brought it, and I ate.”

**66,53,5c** “I am guiltless.”

**66,53,6a** And so they have shown up their own providers as evildoers instead.

**66,53,6b** And indeed it is true.

**66,53,6c** For one who denies God, the maker of all things, ought not, in dissimulation, to be fed from the things of God either.

**66,53,7a** They themselves do not cut the cluster of grapes, but they eat the cluster, so that they are convicted outright of holding drunkenness rather than a grasp of the truth.

**66,53,7b** For which is the more terrible?

**66,53,8** The one who gathers the grapes cut the cluster once, but the one who eats it, with his teeth and by crushing each grape, has tormented and cut it many times over; and the one who has chewed it and consumed it will no longer be like the one who cuts it once.

**66,53,9** But it is only so that they may be seen to make a show — so much proof of truth does the thing hold.

**66,54,1a** Then again he babbles unrestrained about the paradise, which he calls the world.

**66,54,1b** And the plants in it, he says, are the things that are praised among us — which he himself rejects, so that he may be shown to have been truly deceived by the serpent: as the terrible serpent corrupted the hearing of that innocent Eve, so it corrupts his ears too.

**66,54,2a** For the plants spoken of in paradise, he says, are deceptions of desires, which corrupt the reasoning of men.

**66,54,2b** But the plant in paradise from which they learn to recognise what is good is Jesus himself — the knowledge that is in the world.

**66,54,2c** And whoever takes of it distinguishes the good and the evil.

**66,54,3a** And do you see how he twists all that is upright?

**66,54,3b** Yet the apostle cries aloud in plain terms and teaches, “I fear that perhaps, as the serpent beguiled Eve in his cunning, so your thoughts may be corrupted from the purity and the simplicity that is towards Christ.”

**66,54,3c** And see how he declared him a deceiver and crafty and the one who had deceived Eve.

**66,54,4a** And again, in another place, the same apostle writes, “A man should not wear his hair long, since he exists as God’s glory and image.”

**66,54,4b** And do you see how he called hair borne upon a body, and not in a soul, the glory of God?

**66,54,5a** And after this he says, “It was not Adam who was deceived; it was the woman who, having come to be in transgression, has sinned.”

**66,54,5b** “Yet she will find salvation through the bearing of children, if they abide in the faith.”

**66,54,5c** And see how the things that are true by nature have been proclaimed in the divine Scripture, and how vainly he boasts in this way — or rather incurs mockery among those who possess perfect understanding.

**66,54,6a** Then again he relates here that the world does not belong to God, but was fashioned from a portion of matter.

**66,54,6b** But since he does not keep in step with himself, but is carried against his own positions, inventing demolitions and constructions, it is clear to anyone that such a way of thinking is that of a man who raves.

**66,55,1** He also tells of souls being decanted from bodies into bodies — a lie that he is found to have collected perhaps from Plato or from Zeno the Stoic, or from one of those given to fancies.

**66,55,2a** For how is it possible for the soul to be introduced from body into body?

**66,55,2b** If there were bodies already fashioned and ready, and they received the souls in that way, the myth-making of this tragedy would have some plausibility;

**66,55,3a** but if what is sown comes from a small drop, how did the soul come upon so easy a passage in so small a body?

**66,55,3b** For this is how the things that are formed are formed, and his account will no longer hold together.

**66,55,4a** Nor are souls decanted from body into body; for without the union of female with male and of male with female in each kind of living creature, nothing at all that is formed comes into being.

**66,55,4b** Does the soul, then, stand ready in this way, so as to carry out this charlatan’s tragic tale at the joining of the two bodies?

**66,55,5a** Great is the absurdity in those who even entertain such thoughts.

**66,55,5b** But we, so as not to alter what is holy, have thought it enough only to give the outline of the theory, as from a distance.

**66,55,5c** I shall therefore pass on from so corrupting a notion; for all such thoughts are absurd.

**66,55,6a** For if the change of souls is from body into body, and he who was once a man is later a dog, why is a dog not born of a man, or of an ox?

**66,55,6b** Why is no bird brought forth?

**66,55,6c** But if indeed it should happen at some time in the boundless age that some monstrous thing comes to birth, it happens as a sign.

**66,55,7** Nature knows its own limits, and does not change the nature of man by being formed in another way, against nature, nor that of any beast, but in each kind the same kind comes into being.

**66,55,8** And if one body never comes from a body in place of another, how much more will a man’s soul not pass into another body?

**66,55,9a** And to what end, he says, is it changed?

**66,55,9b** So that if ever, when in a man, it did not understand the knowledge of the truth, it may come to be in a dog or in a horse, and when it has been tamed and has understood, return again into a man’s body,

**66,55,10a** and so, having known the knowledge, be taken up into the disc of the moon.

**66,55,10b** And it is a marvel to see that while it was in a man — with whom are schools, grammarians and sophists and untold multitudes of arts, and speech and hearing and learning — the soul remained in ignorance, but when it came to be in a pig it gained knowledge instead; which serves rather to show that his promise of knowledge is a promise for pigs, because of his error and impiety.

**66,56,1** Concerning the fashioning of Adam, the same man, in his account, weaves one thing in place of another into his error, saying that he who said, “Let us make man after our image and likeness” — and he adds the words “Come, let us make,” which is not written; what is written is “Let us make man after our image and likeness.”

**66,56,2** The holy apostle refutes him in what he says, and the Lord himself does so in the gospel, when the Pharisees said to him that it is not good for the man to be all alone, and “Moses said to give a bill of divorce and to put away the wife”; and the Lord, bringing the refutation against the Pharisees,

**66,56,3** said, “Moses wrote according to your hardness of heart, yet from the beginning it did not happen so; rather, the Maker made male and female, and said, ‘For this reason a man will forsake his father and his mother and will cleave to his wife, and the two will become a single flesh,’” and at once he goes on to say,

**66,56,4** “If, then, God has joined together, let man not separate” — confessing that God, that is, his own Father, made Adam and Eve, and that holy marriage was created by him.

**66,56,5** And in keeping with him the holy apostle too, being a herald of the truth, says, “This mystery is great.”

**66,56,6** “But I speak with reference to Christ and the church” — so that from the likeness of what was created by God, Adam and Eve — for God created, and Adam said, “This is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh,

**66,56,7a** and on this account a man will leave,” and that he built the rib into a woman for him — he no longer calls it anything else for him, but a great mystery.

**66,56,7b** And if the fashioning is referred to a man and a woman, but by way of the higher sense is carried through allegory, how, then, does he himself think these things abominable and foreign to the truth of God, blaspheming that what was created by God was created by a ruler, and turning the meaning aside from the truth?

**66,56,8** Then, he says, since from the beginning the soul, torn away from above, causes affliction to the power above, for this reason it sends once for all and plunders from the rulers its own remnant, which is the soul, through these luminaries.

**66,56,9** Great are our hopes and great our expectation, since God, the good, the living and the mighty, has no strength to save — I do not mean his own power that was drawn out of him, but the things that came into being and were fashioned by him — and unless by some other means and by secret robbery he plunders from the heavenly beings the power torn away from him, as this charlatan says, he cannot save us.

**66,57,1a** And why do I still wear myself out, wasting time over his absurdity word by word?

**66,57,1b** For the wretch is not even ashamed to blaspheme by calling him who spoke in the Law and in the Prophets the ruler of darkness.

**66,57,2a** Blessed are our hopes, since Christ, when he came, compelled men to bring offerings to the ruler of darkness!

**66,57,2b** For after cleansing the leper, he, the one who had spoken it, told him to perform the gift written in the Law, saying to the leper cleansed by him, “Go and offer your gift,” “as Moses commanded.”

**66,57,3** And the gift for leprosy was a bird for sacrifice and fine flour for a whole burnt offering.

**66,57,4** But if he were the ruler of darkness, the Word who came from above, the Son of God, who came to turn man back from the error of the rulers, according to Manichaeus’ account, would not have caused the leper he had healed to become subject to him, but would rather have caused him to escape, teaching him not to perform this.

**66,57,5a** But since he had not come to abolish the Law (for he himself had given the Law) nor the Prophets, but to fulfil them, so that he himself might show the undivided devotion of the gospel to be the fulfilment of the Law and the Prophets — that it was one and the same God whom the prophets worshipped, and by him that the Law was given.

**66,57,5b** But now worship is paid to the same God not through the same gifts, but through prayers and thanksgivings and the rest of our observance.

**66,57,6** For to them, as to slaves, he gave burdensome commands, because in that way they could be persuaded; but to those in the gospel lighter ones, as to free men, because of the surpassing greatness of his love for mankind.

**66,57,7** And since there is one God, consistent in both, of the Law and of the gospel, and the service of neither period has been set aside, the same one God is he who reigns over the whole age, served by his servants in each generation, as befits his love for mankind.

**66,57,8** And this man’s error has been refuted on every side, since the Saviour directs that the things of the Law be performed, and, after directing that the things of the Law be performed, releases the things of the Law — not abolishing them but fulfilling them — directing that other offerings be offered to God in place of those in the Law: that is, offerings of piety and goodness, of purity and of conduct.

**66,58,1** Again he says that the Elder will come and show his image in the last days, and then the Omophorus, recognising his face, lets go of the earth, and so the eternal fire consumes the earth.

**66,58,2a** And the brutish man has forgotten himself again, representing as material the earth which a little earlier he said had been created by the Living Spirit.

**66,58,2b** And at the same time he supposes that the whole world is again consumed by the fire.

**66,58,3a** And then, he says, after these things the restoration of the two natures will pass, both together, into the archetype.

**66,58,3b** O great toil, and after the toil nothing brought to amendment!

**66,58,4** For if, after being created and coming into being, it is to be consumed and made to vanish, so that the archetypes may remain again in the sameness of the two natures, good and evil, there will again be a stirring of the evil one to turn back and set war on foot and seize yet another power, so that yet another world comes into being.

**66,58,5** But if this no longer happens, then wickedness will come to its senses, so as no longer to be stirred up against goodness, and the evil god will no longer raise war against the good.

**66,58,6a** And if it is ever brought to its senses, it will not be evil, since it has been altered, turned from its ancient nature of wickedness.

**66,58,6b** And if the nature of evil is changeable, then it certainly changes from evil to good, and a nature that admits a turning to goodness will no longer be evil.

**66,58,6c** For it can be turned even today, and while evil still remains the wicked will be changed into good.

**66,58,7a** And for what reason is he who is going to be turned not turned already?

**66,58,7b** And if it is through God’s devising that the evil one is turned, so as to be no longer able to work evil, then the evil one is no longer responsible for himself, but the good one is, who was able to check his wickedness and did not choose to do before the time the things of the time.

**66,58,8** But if evil is wholly unchangeable, it would never cease making war and being warred upon, and there will never be any settlement of the two natures at all, since evil remains unchangeable and evil is stirred up to display wickedness towards the good and to raise war against goodness.

**66,58,9** And if evil will always be stirred up by desire for the good, then it will no longer be evil, since, longing for the good, he wishes to draw the good to himself, so that, having drawn power to himself through the nature of the good and its full armour, he may think to honour and glorify himself in it, and to embolden and strengthen himself.

**66,58,10** For in everyone who wills the good there is certainly a disposition that springs from a good intention, and the wicked will no longer be wholly wicked when it is found longing for the good.

**66,58,11a** For everything wicked bears hatred towards the good, just as the good does not want the wicked.

**66,58,11b** But if the power of both is mixed together, and the good one knows how to plunder what is his own, to make war and to flay the principalities and the powers, at one time to destroy and do away with the matter produced by the evil one, at another to fashion from it, and at another to do away with it, then wickedness and an incoherent tale is the prattle that this accursed man has brought in upon us.

**66,59,1** Come now, let us speak about the nature of evil too, taking up the argument again: tell us, you there, who have come in the period from the emperor Aurelian to the present and recount the things before all ages — though no prophets anywhere foretold this, nor did the Saviour himself teach it, nor the apostles, unless perhaps you prattle of certain fabricated books under the names of saints, which you set down for yourself and put forward — where, then, have you come from,

**66,59,2a** you there, bringing an ancient-sounding first principle of evil, when you are asked by us whether he says that it is changeable or unchangeable?

**66,59,2b** We have already been told that he presents it as unchangeable, and at one time as changeable and at another as unchangeable: unchangeable towards the wicked, but turning towards the good — so that by both definitions he incurs disgrace before the world.

**66,59,3** For if through many and boundless ages wickedness was unchangeable, having only this very name and nothing else but evil, who, after many ages, turned the unchangeable nature of wickedness so that it turned to what did not belong to it?

**66,59,4** For if it had not yet snatched any power and waged war, nor taken armour for its own strength and for food, but remained without nourishment through many ages, not even needing nourishment, who turned it, which once did not need nourishment, so that it came to nourishment, and sought what it once did not seek, and needed what it once did not need?

**66,59,5a** But if it did after all change its nature, how will your unchangeability of evil be maintained?

**66,59,5b** And if it should come back again to its own state, no longer having anything to eat, how can the evil or wicked one, who has now become accustomed to eating and to using food, endure for the time to come, continuing without food?

**66,59,6** For if, when he had not yet become accustomed to foods, he could not hold out, but was turned to come to food, and plundered the soul and got it for himself as food, much more, now that he has become accustomed to food, will he be unrestrainable in his nature, and nothing could persuade him, once he has become greedy and has had experience of food, to continue without these things, as your account, incoherent as it is, would have it.

**66,60,1** But I shall pass over this topic, and carry my account on again to other parts of his drivel.

**66,60,2a** For again he says that the rulers will then be in their own portions, and the Father will take back his own portions.

**66,60,2b** Who, then, is this equitable one, to measure out the boundary of each portion on either side?

**66,60,2c** And how will he be persuaded who from the beginning would not obey the truth and the good?

**66,60,2d** And if the good one should by compulsion persuade the lawless one to keep to his own and not to trespass on the good one’s share, why could he not do this from the beginning, before his portions were plundered from him at all?

**66,60,3a** And how will the two be together, each possessing a portion?

**66,60,3b** For if he has portions at all, and the other portions are not his, the Almighty will no longer be called almighty, no longer God of all things, and the evil one will no longer become subject to the good, but each of them has his own dominion.

**66,60,4a** And of what will the evil one be master, when the world no longer exists, nor the living creatures and men ruled by him?

**66,60,4b** And if he is evil, and matter, and corruption at all, why has he not rather been corrupted?

**66,60,4c** For if wickedness, existing from that time, was corruption, and corrupts other things but does not corrupt itself, then that which corrupts other things is no longer itself subject to corruption, remaining everlasting and not vanishing.

**66,60,5a** And while it remains in solid substance, corrupting other things and not itself, it can leave nothing alone; rather, the corruption of the others will in any case corrupt the others.

**66,60,5b** And if its substance endures, it will no longer leave anything that exists, but it alone will remain, and the things corrupted through it vanish.

**66,60,6a** But if it is evil to itself as well, and corruption to itself, its substance will no longer stand.

**66,60,6b** Not only in the future, I would say, but it would have vanished from that time on, having already corrupted itself within itself and vanished.

**66,60,7a** But all these are the tales of the senseless man’s idle talk; when you have observed them, you understanding sons of the holy church of God and of the faith of the Lord, see through the charlatan and laugh his drivel to scorn.

**66,60,7b** He will, however, return to the pretexts he has wickedly devised for himself, and to likenesses drawn from the divine Scriptures, which do not mean this, but are wickedly understood in this way by him.

**66,60,8** Come, then, let us set them out word for word — the passages that he filches from the divine Scriptures, as I said, and expounds according to his own mind — even though we have very often taken up these same passages and refuted them most thoroughly.

**66,61,1a** First, then: finding in the divine Scriptures the name of the Paraclete, and not knowing the power of the holy Paraclete, he slipped himself in, supposing himself to be this.

**66,61,1b** And he claims that the words spoken by the holy Paul have yielded place to him, inasmuch as the holy apostle said, “It is in part that we know, and in part that we prophesy.”

**66,61,1c** “When the perfect comes, what is in part will be done away.”

**66,61,2** But the holy apostle, who together with his fellow apostles was deemed worthy of the Holy Spirit himself, does not set this out about the Paraclete at all;

**66,61,3a** rather he was speaking of the two worlds, the present and the future, as I said, telling those who wished to grasp matters of the times, “Let nothing alarm you, in word or in letter, as though the day of the Lord had come.”

**66,61,3b** “For unless the son of lawlessness is revealed, the man of unrighteousness,” and the rest.

**66,61,4** And again, when the disciples had come together to the Saviour, they kept asking him about the consummation, and he said to them, “It is not yours to know times and seasons which the Father has fixed by his own authority; but you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you.”

**66,61,5** And again he said, “Do not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Spirit, which you have heard” — that is, the Spirit, the Paraclete, of whom he said, “If I go away, he will come, and will declare all things to you.”

**66,61,6** And the words “he will declare all things to you” refer to the gift of which they were to be counted worthy — that the Holy Spirit would dwell in them, so as to set out plainly for them all things, as many as they could contain in this age.

**66,61,7** And here in this age, having received the Spirit, the Paraclete, they prophesied — as “Agabus prophesied that there would be a famine,” and “prophets came down from Jerusalem,” and “Philip had four daughters who prophesied.”

**66,61,8** But whenever they prophesy, it is in part that they prophesy and in part that they know, and the perfect they await, hoping for it in the ages to come, “when what is perishable has been changed into imperishability and what is mortal into immortality, when, then, it is face to face.”

**66,61,9a** For now things are seen in a riddle, but there is prepared what eye has not seen here.

**66,61,9b** There perfection is revealed, the things that ear has not heard here.

**66,61,9c** There is the great gift for the saints, which here has not come up into the heart of man.

**66,61,10a** And you see that the knowledge of things beyond the ordinary was not stored up for Mani.

**66,61,10b** For how could Mani know, when he failed in his own aim?

**66,61,10c** For he set out to bring Marcellus under his hand.

**66,61,10d** He came against Archelaus to defeat him, and was not able.

**66,61,11a** How, then, can one who did not know what was close at hand know about greater things?

**66,61,11b** And how did he not escape the hands of the king of the Persians, when he was caught and paid the penalty? It was so that he might be exposed, to those who have understanding, as lying in everything.

**66,62,1** Again he wishes to bring testimony, so as to establish what he calls the dyad and to make an empty division between the two principles, from the Saviour’s saying, “A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a rotten tree bear good fruit; for the tree is known by its fruit.”

**66,62,2a** And see, I pray you, the shallow mind that understands nothing of the divine Scripture in depth.

**66,62,2b** For if they are trees, then they also have a husbandman, and being plants they have certainly been planted by someone.

**66,62,2c** And everything that has been planted is not without beginning, but has a beginning.

**66,62,2d** And having a beginning it will also undergo an end.

**66,62,3a** So the rotten tree did not always exist, but was planted; nor is this good tree described with regard to the whole goodness from above.

**66,62,3b** For in that place there is goodness without falsehood, admitting no change, and the thought of the holy God who is, in ineffable honour.

**66,62,4a** But as regards the working of plants, let us see whether it is so, and let us take it up and speak.

**66,62,4b** For if the saying is about the devil, we have already shown many times that he was not made evil.

**66,62,4c** For God made nothing base, and this is quite plain to those of understanding.

**66,62,5a** For if we are returning to the same matters, there will be no harm in demonstrating the account of the truth on the present occasion as well.

**66,62,5b** In the beginning, then, he was not base, but he turned out base.

**66,62,5c** See, the argument about the plant will not hold on this point.

**66,62,6a** For we see Saul too, who became a persecutor, yet afterwards suffered persecution on behalf of the name he once persecuted.

**66,62,6b** We see Judas chosen with the twelve apostles, and later turning out ill and ranked in an evil portion.

**66,62,7a** We see Rahab the harlot, who was a stranger to the race of Israel, but later repented and received God’s mercy.

**66,62,7b** We see the robber, caught in crime and hanged on the tree, who confessed and entered paradise together with the Lord.

**66,62,7c** We see Nicolaus, who was good and chosen, but later turned out evil and was ranked among the heresiarchs.

**66,62,8a** And why should I tell the multitudes?

**66,62,8b** What, then, is this evil plant from which good does not come?

**66,62,8c** Why, once more, they are the deeds of men.

**66,62,8d** For goodness cannot come from fornication; righteousness cannot come from the envy of wickedness; praise cannot arise from adultery.

**66,62,9** For the very tree of sin cannot arise by means of goodness — which is to say, a wicked tree does not produce good fruits, nor can wicked fruits come of a good tree.

**66,62,10** For example, the good tree that does not bear evil fruit is hospitality when it is practised — and whatever may come of hospitality, its force is not for the sake of baseness — almsgiving, purity for God’s sake, continence for the Master’s sake, righteousness for the Law’s sake.

**66,62,11a** This, then, is how these two trees stand, concerning righteousness and concerning sin.

**66,62,11b** But as for what this barbarian Mani has in mind, he means to say that they concern God and the devil.

**66,62,12** And that no one can dare to say of God that he will ever do evil — far from it — nor of the devil that he works good, this is plain.

**66,62,13a** But all good things come about through God, and nothing base has been created by him, nor comes about.

**66,62,13b** And if certain evils are worked by the devil, see, we have found that even through him a crown is woven for the saints and a prize given to those who have conquered.

**66,62,14a** And his argument has collapsed.

**66,62,14b** For the rotten tree and the good tree concern good works and base ones.

**66,62,14c** And it is not about the Old Testament and the New, as Mani’s account would have it.

**66,63,1a** Further, the same man, wishing to establish his pretexts about the two principles, goes hunting for the texts that suit him, which run as follows: that, he says, he said to the Jews, “You are sons of the devil.”

**66,63,1b** “That one was a killer of men, for his father was a liar.”

**66,63,2** And he means to blaspheme by saying that the devil’s father is the maker of heaven and earth, though this saying can in no way at all be applied to him.

**66,63,3a** For if they are sons of the devil at all, his own account has collapsed, and Mani fights against himself without knowing it.

**66,63,3b** For their souls have then been marked off as born of the devil, and are no longer from the power above, according to his myth, nor are they part of the light, or of its armour, or of the Pillar of Light, or of the Mother of Life.

**66,63,4** And if they are of the devil at all, then Abraham too, their father, whose seed the Jews themselves are, is himself also of the devil, according to Mani’s account.

**66,63,5a** How, then, does the Saviour say to them by way of reproof, “You are not children of Abraham, but of your father the devil.”

**66,63,5b** “For if you were children of Abraham, you would do his works.”

**66,63,5c** “For you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth to you.”

**66,63,5d** “This Abraham did not do.”

**66,63,6a** And you see that the expression is used loosely; for they were sons of Abraham, and the Lord estranges them by reason of their works, not by reason of their formation or of their making.

**66,63,6b** We have already spoken of this above as well.

**66,63,6c** How, then, will a part of the same seed be at one time alien and of the devil, and at another a part of God?

**66,63,7a** But he says this by way of accusation.

**66,63,7b** For to whomever a man subjects himself, of him he is the slave, in conduct and in teaching, as Paul too says, “For though you have many teachers, yet you have not many fathers.”

**66,63,7c** “For in Christ Jesus I begot you through the gospel.”

**66,63,8a** And do you see that he means the teaching?

**66,63,8b** Had Mani received Abraham, we might have said that Abraham belonged to the God of light, and those begotten by him to another.

**66,63,9a** But the matter stands in this way.

**66,63,9b** They imitated the murderer, they imitated the betrayal of Judas, they took up the slander of the traitor, they became sons of his denial of God; he became a liar, holding the money-box and stealing, and saying to him, “Hail, Rabbi.”

**66,63,9c** And he was reproved, and heard, “Friend, for what have you come?”

**66,63,10a** This Judas imitated Cain — since Cain became a murderer, lying before the Lord and saying, “Am I my brother’s keeper?”

**66,63,10b** “I do not know where he is.”

**66,63,10c** And he too became a son by imitation, and by his contemplation of the false-speaking voice which spoke in the serpent and said, “You will be like gods, knowing good and evil.”

**66,63,11a** This is what was said in the gospel by the Saviour, “You are sons of the devil.”

**66,63,11b** For he says, “Did I not choose you twelve?”

**66,63,11c** “One of you is a devil.”

**66,63,11d** “Since from the beginning he is a liar and a killer of men, for his father was a liar.”

**66,63,12a** And the question this man raises has been resolved.

**66,63,12b** For the Jews were not children of the devil — far from it.

**66,63,12c** For the Samaritan woman says to the Saviour, “Here on this mountain our fathers worshipped, and you for your part say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem.”

**66,63,13a** Then, after much more, the Saviour said to her, “We speak what we know, for salvation is from the Jews.”

**66,63,13b** And again the apostle: “It is evident that the Lord has sprung from Judah.”

**66,63,13c** And there is much to say on this and to refute this man’s error.

**66,64,1** Again he seizes on this text, “The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overtake it,” saying that the darkness was pursuing the light, as the evil rulers pursue and make war on the Godhead.

**66,64,2a** But if the light, being warred upon, is pursued by the darkness, then the darkness is stronger than the light, since the light flees from the face of the darkness and does not venture to stand and show itself, because the darkness is stronger.

**66,64,2b** But it is not so.

**66,64,3a** For the light does not flee before the darkness, but “the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overtake it.”

**66,64,3b** And if darkness did not overtake the light, this differs widely from the mind of Mani, who says that it not only overtook it but even snatched armour from it.

**66,64,3c** How, then, did that which by his announcement had snatched armour not overtake the light at all?

**66,64,3d** And how does the light, if it is pursued, shine of its own free choice in the darkness?

**66,64,4** But since the minds of men had been darkened by the clouding of sin, God first sent the Law, giving light as by a lamp shining alongside,

**66,64,5a** as Peter says in his epistle, “Attending to the prophetic word as to a lamp shining in a squalid place, until the Morning Star rises and day dawns in your hearts.”

**66,64,5b** For from then on the light shines in the darkness — the Law, given in the hand of a mediator, through Moses, the faithful servant of God.

**66,64,6** This is why, since from the earliest times the light was first shining like a spark in the natural law — the light which Enoch beheld and was well-pleasing to the Lord, by which Abel was guided and was well-pleasing to the Lord, by which Noah found favour before God, because he perceived the way, by which Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.

**66,64,7** Then the light, passing on from the manner of a spark, added the brightness of a lamp that appeared in a squalid place — that is, “the light shines in the darkness”: the commandment of God, and the mind set on goodness, giving light in the heart of the faithful amid the clouded thinking of the base and evil deeds that had arisen among men, idolatry and denial of God, murders and adultery and the rest.

**66,64,8** And when the great luminary came, “the true light, which enlightens every man coming into the world, was in the world, and the world came into being through him, and the world did not know him — he who came to his own, and his own did not receive him; yet to all who received him he gave authority to become children of God.”

**66,64,9a** And do you see in what darkness this light shines, and what darkness did not overtake it?

**66,64,9b** It is that the good, ever sent by God to the minds of men and giving light in the world, has not been overcome by sin.

**66,65,1a** In like manner the same Mani again seizes on the Saviour’s saying, “The kingdom of heaven is like a householder who sowed his field with good seed.”

**66,65,1b** “And as the men were sleeping, a man who was an enemy came and sowed tares.”

**66,65,2a** “Then his servants say to him, ‘Did you not sow good seed in the field?’”

**66,65,2b** “And he said, ‘Yes.’”

**66,65,2c** “‘Where, then, do the tares come from?’”

**66,65,2d** “And he answered and said, ‘An enemy has done this.’”

**66,65,2e** “And the servants said to him, ‘Do you want us, then, to go and root up the tares?’”

**66,65,3a** “But he said to them, ‘No, lest in rooting up the tares you root up the wheat as well.’”

**66,65,3b** “‘But let them be until harvest time, and I will tell the reapers: collect the tares and tie them in bundles, store the wheat in the granary, and get the tares ready to be burned up with unquenchable fire.’”

**66,65,4** And when his disciples in the house said, “Explain to us the parable of the tares,” he unfolds it and does not pass judgement, so as not to allow the deceiver to gain a hold against the truth.

**66,65,5a** So the Lord answers plainly and says, “He who sowed the good seed is God.”

**66,65,5b** “The field is the world, and the tares are the evil men; the hostile man is the devil; and the reapers are the angels, and the harvest is the end of the age, and the wheat is the good men.”

**66,65,6** When the Lord gives the command to his angels, they gather the sinners out of his kingdom and hand them over to be burned.

**66,65,7a** And observe, sons of the truth, that the very things he means to say are put forward against himself by this man, who has been renewed for us in place of Jannes and Jambres.

**66,65,7b** For he denies that the world belongs to God; but here the Saviour said that the field is the world, and that the householder is the lord of the field, that is, his own Father, and that he himself had sown his good seed;

**66,65,8a** nor did he divide the souls from the bodies, or the bodies from the souls; rather, he said that the enemy man had sown the tares, and these are the evil men.

**66,65,8b** And by men he does not mean bodies on their own, but he spoke of wicked men as a whole.

**66,65,9a** And again, in the same way, the householder sowed the good seed in his own field — the good men, he says.

**66,65,9b** And it was not their souls he named, but good men, with body and soul.

**66,65,10** So, then, through teaching God sows the good in men, and through his evil contriving the devil sows evil works among men by stealth.

**66,65,11a** On this side and on that we shall find no root of wickedness, but works carried out through us; and the devil is not at all the cause of the tares that were sown.

**66,65,11b** For at once he makes it clear by saying, “while men slept,” and he did not say “while the householder slept.”

**66,65,11c** For when we fall asleep and leave off good works, when we neglect righteousness, when we do not keep our mind awake to the commandment of God, then we are sown with sins.

**66,65,12a** Do you see that the reapers make the bundles ready for the eternal fire?

**66,65,12b** Tell me, Mani, do they bind souls there, or do they burn bodies together with the soul, or the souls as well?

**66,65,12c** For your account of the purification of the souls will no longer stand, when they are to be handed over to punishment and judgement.

**66,65,12d** But this will suffice on these matters for the present.

**66,65,12e** For to those of understanding the sayings of the truth are plain.

**66,66,1a** Again he seizes on another text and brings it forward, and, not understanding what is contained in it, he misinterprets and turns aside the force of the saving teaching, because the Saviour said, “The ruler of this world is coming, and finds nothing of his in me.”

**66,66,1b** And again, in the apostle’s words, “The god of this age blinded the thoughts of the unbelievers, so that the illumination of the gospel of the glory should not shine forth.”

**66,66,2a** Let us see, then, whether the ruler of this world — the one the Lord is speaking of — “will be cast down.”

**66,66,2b** “But if I am lifted up, I will draw all to myself”: whom does he call the ruler of this world?

**66,66,2c** And if he means the devil, how does John in the gospel say of the Saviour that he came to his own?

**66,66,3a** For we see these two expressions set in opposition to each other.

**66,66,3b** For the apostle says, “The whole world lies in evil,” and the Saviour was in the world.

**66,66,3c** How, then, are both to be reconciled?

**66,66,3d** If the whole world lies in evil, what place is there for the Saviour in the world, that he should be in the world?

**66,66,4a** And if the things of the world belong to the Son of God as his own, what sort of ruler has lordship over God’s own possessions?

**66,66,4b** But if what is in the world does not belong to the Son of God as his own, what kind of ruler of the world would concede that the things in the world were the Saviour’s own?

**66,66,4c** And if the world belongs to the Son of God, how could he permit a ruler to keep possession of a world that is his own?

**66,66,5a** But all the words of the divine Scripture have been spoken in wisdom, even as the Lord himself declares, “John came in the way of righteousness, not eating and not drinking, and people say, ‘He has a demon.’”

**66,66,5b** “The Son of Man came both eating and drinking, and people say, ‘Look, a gluttonous man and a wine-drinker, a friend of tax-collectors and sinners’; and wisdom was justified by her children.”

**66,66,6a** And in what way was wisdom justified by her children?

**66,66,6b** Why, by those who understand the words of wisdom, as he says in the prophet too, “Who is wise, and will understand these things?”

**66,66,6c** “For straight are the ways of the Lord, and he who has a word of wisdom will also know these things, but the ungodly will grow weak in them.”

**66,67,1a** For he has in truth grown weak and acted impiously, together with the ungodly, in the divine and heavenly words.

**66,67,1b** For a little before, the Saviour said, “I beheld Satan fallen like lightning from heaven.”

**66,67,1c** And here again: “The ruler of this world will be cast down.”

**66,67,2a** And if the saying was about Satan, who had already fallen, what need was there for him to be cast down again?

**66,67,2b** But you will surely say: into the abyss.

**66,67,2c** Where, then, was the Lord to be lifted up?

**66,67,2d** For if he was to be lifted up from the abyss, then like set alongside like would make the expression balanced.

**66,67,2e** But when was he lifted up on the earth?

**66,67,3** For he was speaking of the lifting up of the cross and of his going up into heaven, that he might draw all up to himself.

**66,67,4a** And for what reason, being above, did he not draw them, but came to the earth?

**66,67,4b** For he had to come and take the form of men upon himself, so that first that very holy vessel which he took from Mary — God the Word from above, coming from the bosom of the Father, having formed the holy body for himself — so that, lifted up in his own body [to lift up in it], he might draw those like him to himself.

**66,67,5a** And who is this world’s ruler?

**66,67,5b** Why, as he says, “The whole world lies in evil” — meaning not heaven, not the earth, not sun, not moon, not plants, not sea, not mountains, not air, not clouds, not wind, not stars, not birds, nothing at all of the things created, far from it, but the world of men: the pride of their thinking, the boldness of their conceit, the arrogance of men’s self-exaltation — this ruler of this world fell down through pride.

**66,67,6** “For you,” he says, “receive glory from one another, but I do not seek my own glory.”

**66,67,7a** For how did pride not fall?

**66,67,7b** How was the ruler of the world not shattered, when Herod held in custody and judged the judge of the living and the dead and the Lord, when Pilate presided, an officer struck his cheek, Judas betrayed him, Caiaphas sat in judgement, Jews spat on him, and soldiers beat the head of him who could roll up heaven and earth with a nod?

**66,67,8a** This pride and boldness and glory of worldly men — that was the ruler of the world, the one who fell to the ground.

**66,67,8b** For all who hold eminence in the dignities of this world have their rule through haughty snorting, through boldness and renown and pride, none of which has been found in the Saviour.

**66,67,8c** For “a smouldering wick he will not quench, and a bruised reed he will not break.”

**66,68,1a** And I have much to say on this.

**66,68,1b** Again the same Mani says, “The god,” he says, “of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelievers, so that they should not see clearly into the illumination of the gospel.”

**66,68,2** If there is a god of this world, what, then, was the Saviour doing in coming into what belonged to another?

**66,68,3** And if he coveted what belonged to another, this is not the act of one who is good, nor of one who is just; but if he came to save what was not his own but another’s, this too is the act of some flatterer who wants to entice away his neighbour’s people.

**66,68,4a** And if he came to save the things of the god of this age at all, then he is laying up a favour with the god of the world himself, by trying to save his own vessels.

**66,68,4b** And if the god of this age consents at all to the saving of his own through the Saviour, then he is good, even if he cannot save, since he rejoices at the salvation of his own.

**66,68,5a** And there will then be one partnership in goodness: the one who is able saves, and the one who is unable to save his own rejoices at those who are saved, counting it gain to have his own saved by the one who saves well.

**66,68,5b** And if he does not oppose at all the one who wishes to save his own, he will also acknowledge his gratitude.

**66,68,6a** But if he acknowledges gratitude, then he first saves the one to whom those being saved belong, so as to show his goodness towards him in saving him.

**66,68,6b** And he does not prefer to save the little ones and leave aside the principal one, from whom those being saved have come into being.

**66,68,7a** Or again, to put it otherwise: if he chooses not to save him, but saves those under him, then he does not accomplish a perfect work, nor can he work the good in perfection.

**66,68,7b** But if, because he is of a nature that is not saved, he is unable to save him, but saves those who have come into being from him, much more are those who have come into being from him more rotten than he, and incapable of salvation.

**66,68,8** And besides, if, having nothing of his own to save, he came into what belonged to another for the sake of display, to show his help, great is the helplessness that cannot save its own and goes abroad into what belongs to others, so as to exhibit the work that it was unable to exhibit among its own.

**66,68,9a** And the account given by Mani about the Saviour and the ruler of this age has already collapsed; and there is in reality a god of this age — not another god differing from him who is, nor another god with a real subsistence, far from it.

**66,68,9b** For God, the Master of all, who made the world, is one God — Father of our Lord Jesus Christ — who never ceases.

**66,69,1** But concerning the one of whom the apostle speaks, whom the unbelievers chose to have as their own god, I say that the god of this age is not one only, far from it, but many, to whom the unbelievers have subjected themselves and have been blinded in their understanding, as he says in another place too,

**66,69,2a** “whose god is the belly, and their glory is in their shame.”

**66,69,2b** And the Lord in the gospel says, “You cannot serve two masters.”

**66,69,2c** Then, after much more, to show who the two masters are, he says, “You cannot serve God and mammon.”

**66,69,3a** So, then, God is God, and mammon is a god of the world.

**66,69,3b** For through these two, mammon and the belly, the greater part of mankind is blinded, being enticed — not taking the occasion from God, but through its own evil contriving, as each one, in his craving, gives himself up through unbelief as subject to everything.

**66,69,4a** Hence the apostle too says, “Of all evils the root is love of money.”

**66,69,4b** And for this reason he lays a curse on the evil preconception that makes a god of it, saying, “Foods for the belly and the belly for foods, but God will do away with both the one and the other,” cursing the desires of the stomach.

**66,69,5a** So the god of this age blinded the minds of the unbelievers, as in the gospel too the scribe is found, first and second, saying, “By doing what am I to inherit eternal life?”

**66,69,5b** And he said, “Honour your father and mother, according to what is written.”

**66,69,5c** For the things of the Law were not foreign.

**66,69,5d** Likewise the Lord teaches that the keeping of the Law is the inheritance of life.

**66,69,6a** Then he says, “All these I have done from my youth.”

**66,69,6b** And on hearing it he rejoiced, to show that the commandments of the Law are not foreign to his Godhead.

**66,69,6c** For by saying that he rejoiced, he made the Old Testament agree with the New Testament.

**66,69,7a** But he says, “What do I still lack?”

**66,69,7b** And he says to him, “If you wish to become perfect, sell what you have and give it to the poor, and take your cross and follow me, and you will have treasure in the heavens.”

**66,69,7c** “But he went away grieving.”

**66,69,7d** “For he was very rich.”

**66,69,7e** Next the Lord declared, “A camel will find it easier to pass through a needle’s eye than a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.”

**66,69,7f** For he is unable to enter, since the god of the age has blinded them, and they hold mammon to be their god and have made themselves subject to the god of this age, that is, to the love of money.

**66,69,9a** As he says, “Be on your guard against the Pharisees’ leaven, which is hypocrisy,” and elsewhere, “which is love of money.”

**66,69,9b** And to show its outcome and its work, he says, “They are blind guides.”

**66,69,9c** “And when a blind man guides a blind man, both will fall into a pit.”
